newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil deputy presents bill to open energy sectors.
newsitem.headline: Brazil deputy presents bill to open energy sectors.

text.p: A bill regulating the opening up of Brazil's oil and gas industries would end fuel subisidies and allow the private sector to import fuel three years after its approval, a lawmaker in charge of writing the legislation said.

A draft of Dep. Eliseu Resende's bill, which was read to a Chamber of Deputies on Tuesday, also sets down rules for the creation of a new regulator to oversee competition between state giant Petrobras and private competition.
Resende said the bill, which provides the small print of a constitutional amendment passed in 1995 to end Brazil's state oil and gas monopolies, would create "an open and competitive market."
The new regulator, called the National Petroleum Agency (ANP), would be up and running, at least in preliminary form, 120 days after the bill is approved by Congress, Resende said.

Directors of the ANP would be named by the Brazilian president and ratified by the Senate. The upper house would also have to approve the dismissal of ANP directors before the end of their terms, Resende said.

Unlike an original draft of the legislation written by the Mines and Energy Ministry, Resende's version did not contemplate the creation of a government-controlled council to determine oil and gas policy.

Instead, the deputy's bill forsaw a policy-making council which would set policy for the entire energy sector and would have powers, in extreme circumstances such as war, to restore government control over the energy industries.
Subsidies to make fuel affordable in distant regions of Brazil would be allowed after the initial three-year transition period, but would have to be approved by Congress, Resende said.

The new legislation would entitle Petrobras to maintain the areas where it is currently producing or exploring for oil and gas but those concessions must be registered with the ANP and may be transfered to other companies with ANP approval.
The agency would be responsible for tendering out concessions for exploration rights in other areas.

The lower house committee has until next week to propose alterations to the bill and may then begin voting. If approved by the panel, the legislation advances to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies and then to committee-level discussions in the Senate.
